args.message: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` while the docstring (and `tests/test_money.py`, per FIN-212) requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail on `test_half_even`.

## Change
- Switch the quantize rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed (including `tests/test_money.py`).
args.head: fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212
args.title: Fix banker's rounding in round_money (FIN-212)

2. **Fixed on a new branch** `fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212`: changed `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212 (commit `08d3cd5986`).

transcript.reasoning_content: Let me look at the files.

transcript.content: The bug is clear: `src/money.py` uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` instead of `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Let me fix it on a new branch.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Fix: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Note 2.675 -> 2.68 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN: 2.675 is not exactly representable; Decimal("2.675") is exact decimal 2.675, quantize to 2.68 since 7 is odd? ROUND_HALF_EVEN on 2.675 -> 2.68 (last digit 7 is odd, so round up to 8, even). 2.665 -> 2.66 (6 already even). Correct.

Create branch, commit, run CI.
